<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **33** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8ae0ab9b0d77d56473e89dae9fe437778172dda8`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`, `ObjectSchema (symbol, 45 pages)`, `master_detail (literal, 40 pages)`, `owner_id (literal, 38 pages)`
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8ae0ab9b0d77d56473e89dae9fe437778172dda8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8d13c8f5326e373bb1769db64485f79e55da19f2` — the merge of head `1899fc5e98d39bbf682d4c71d9dfa33b5a0dc9fc` into base `8ae0ab9b0d77d56473e89dae9fe437778172dda8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8d13c8f5326e373bb1769db64485f79e55da19f2 && git checkout 8d13c8f5326e373bb1769db64485f79e55da19f2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8ae0ab9b0d77d56473e89dae9fe437778172dda8 1899fc5e98d39bbf682d4c71d9dfa33b5a0dc9fc && git checkout -B drift-repro 8ae0ab9b0d77d56473e89dae9fe437778172dda8 && git merge --no-ff 1899fc5e98d39bbf682d4c71d9dfa33b5a0dc9fc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8ae0ab9b0d77d56473e89dae9fe437778172dda8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8ae0ab9b0d77d56473e89dae9fe437778172dda8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `469499edc7c7e84a9bc8de5b96b0f47f0ec85c9e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/conversions/refused-shapes.ts, packages/spec/src/data/controlled-by-parent-master.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/readable-ids-conformance.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.cbp-optional-master-admitted.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template, docs/adr/0055-master-detail-controlled-by-parent.md + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-cbp-read-filter.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-cbp-relation.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-read-filter.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts (read, unchanged), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts (read, unchanged), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/controlled-by-parent-optional-master.test.ts, packages/lint/src/data-model-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-readable-ids-permission-formula.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/entries/18/cbp-master-detail-required-defaulted.ts (read, unchanged), scripts/adr-anchors/packages__plugins__plugin-security__src__security-plugin-cbp-read-filter.ts.json, scripts/adr-anchors/packages__plugins__plugin-security__src__security-plugin-cbp-relation.ts.json, scripts/adr-anchors/packages__plugins__plugin-security__src__security-plugin.ts.json, scripts/adr-anchors/packages__spec__src__data__object.zod.ts.json (read, unchanged), .changeset/30905-cbp-optional-master.md, the five `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/**` test files of commit 469499ed

Reviewed against: card #30905 (body), claim 6685806956, dev report 6685276956, ruling record 6687830530 (option A: at the raw parse doors a cbp master with `required` omitted reads as optional; builder, stored rows and Studio still default to required; `os lint` errors on the omission), spec consent 6688103341, the PR body, ADR-0055 on `main` and on the head. Diff read whole against the merge base `1b3e22f0` (40 files, +1650 / -231). Head confirmed on the PR at the time of writing.

### ① Derived judgments

**Must-fix**

1. **Four ADR anchors still state the pre-amendment §1 rule as a "Do NOT" instruction.** `scripts/adr-anchors/packages__plugins__plugin-security__src__security-plugin-cbp-read-filter.ts.json`, `…security-plugin-cbp-relation.ts.json`, `…security-plugin.ts.json` and `scripts/adr-anchors/packages__spec__src__data__object.zod.ts.json` each carry the ADR-0055 invariant "derives a `controlled_by_parent` object's master from exactly one `master_detail` field declared `required: true` … and from nothing else: zero such fields … resolve `null`" and, for `object.zod.ts`, "no such field (a non-required `master_detail`, …) at `sharingModel` … do NOT accept a second tier here (any `master_detail`, …)". On this head the code those anchors bind resolves the only `master_detail` declared `required: false` as the optional master (`security-plugin-cbp-relation.ts:169-181`, `object.zod.ts:4109` via `controlled-by-parent-master.ts:168-179`) and the ADR is amended to say so. `check-adr-anchors.mjs` is a presence check by design (its header: "the failure text carries the INVARIANT"), so CI stays green while the invariant it hands the next author now contradicts the amended ADR and the code — the exact hazard the ADR's own 2026-09-07 amendment names ("an ADR recording a narrower enforcement than the runtime performs errs in the unsafe direction for reviewers"). Fix: in each of the four files, amend the ADR-0055 sentence to §1 as amended (one `master_detail` declared `required: true`, or, with none, the object's only `master_detail` declared `required: false` — an optional master whose null-master rows are read by the row's owner and by View All on the detail through the one chokepoint; an omitted `required` on an unparsed object still resolves none), keeping the "do NOT restore the retired tiers (any `master_detail`, a required `lookup`, first-by-field-order)" instruction, which still holds. Not a governed path; no Tier H needed for it.

2. **The ADR amendment records a ruled question as open.** `docs/adr/0055-master-detail-controlled-by-parent.md:211`: "Whether the parse should tell the two spellings apart is the maintainer's open question on #30905 (letters A, B and C); this amendment records option A, the one the code implements, and decides nothing further." The maintainer ruled A on that question at 14:57Z on 2026-11-06 (record 6687830530 on #30905), before this head was pushed. The ADR is the Tier H record the maintainer approves by hand; it must say the question was ruled, and cite the record. Fix: replace the sentence with one that names ruling record 6687830530 (option A) as the decision this bullet implements — the rest of the bullet is accurate as written.

**Should-fix** (for the seat; none blocks on its own)

3. `packages/spec/src/conversions/entries/18/cbp-master-detail-required-defaulted.ts:56-67` (unchanged, on the claim's ⛔ list) still says the builder refuses an explicit `required: false` and that a live author "still meets the parse's refusal"; both are false for the sole master under ruling A. The dev reported it (out-of-scope finding c). One sentence in this PR with the seat's consent, or in #30907.
4. `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts:2042-2068`: on a withheld null-master row the narration says "it has no owner (a queue row), so View All alone reads it" whenever `record.owner_id == null`. On an object with no `owner_id` column that is every row, and such a row is not a queue row. Narration only; the verdict is the read door's. Could read "it carries no owner" when `CbpRelation.ownerColumn` is false.
5. Studio cannot author an optional master and the OWD overview shows none for one (`owd-sharing.ts` `deriveMasterObject` reads `required === true`); `os db orphans` skips optional-master details (`orphan-detail-sweep.ts`). Both already in the seat's findings list on record 6687830530; recorded here so the carrier is not lost.

**Confirmed** (file:line on the head)

- *The one read chokepoint.* `security-plugin-cbp-read-filter.ts:109-184` is the only place that builds the cbp read answer; every door composes it and none builds an arm of its own: the authz middleware for the caller and, on a delegated read, the delegator (`security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts:2361`, `:2380`, each pushed into the same `extra` that carries the Layer-0 tenant wall, `:2347-2349`, and AND-ed); `getReadFilter` (`security-plugin-read-filter.ts:159`, AND-ed with `computeRlsFilter`, which carries the wall, and the sharing layer, `:164`) — the door analytics, the engine's `ReadableIds` composer (attachments, comments, activity, approvals, and every chain hop) and search/export reach; the delegated read filter for the delegate and the delegator (`:234`, `:236`). The three hosts in `security-plugin.ts:2218`, `:2898`, `:2955` forward the new argument; the private method `:4878-4900` adds `permissionEvaluator` to the host. `git grep` on the head finds no other caller.
- *The arms.* `:159`: a required master returns `masterArm`, the same object literal as before (`{ [fk]: { $in: ReadableIds.of(master) } }`) — no `$or`; pinned by "a REQUIRED master answers the leaf it always did" (`controlled-by-parent-optional-master.test.ts:987-997`). `:178-184`: for an optional master the null arm is `{ fk: null }` for a holder of View All on the detail, else `{ $and: [{ fk: null }, { owner_id: caller }] }` when the registered schema carries `owner_id` (`CbpRelation.ownerColumn`, `security-plugin-cbp-relation.ts:181`, `:226`), else no arm. A row with a set fk is matched by the master arm alone (`$in` never matches null); a null fk never by the master arm; a null fk with a null owner matches nobody but View All; an object without `owner_id` grants nothing on the null arm. `hasSuperuserReadBypass` is `viewAllRecords`/`modifyAllRecords` on the object (`permission-evaluator.ts:475-481`, bit `view`); its `isPrivate` option is documented as never changing that vote (`:452`), so omitting it here is not a divergence from `security-plugin-rls-filter.ts:183`/`:374`.
- *Fail-closed order kept.* The deny sentinel for an unresolved relation (`:130`) and the `$in: []` cycle/depth answers (`:139-156`) return before the optional branch, so a refused chain denies null-master rows too, as the ADR says.
- *Verbs.* `CBP_LEAF_READ_VERBS` = find, findOne, count, aggregate (`:83`): count and aggregate carry the `$or`; a write verb's predicate is still answered `null`.
- *Engine composition of the new shape.* The engine composes `ReadableIds` leaves inside `$or` arms (`engine-readable-ids-composition.test.ts:302-308`, `engine-readable-ids-nested-composition.test.ts:388-393`), and a chain's intermediate level with an optional master answers its `getReadFilter` as the `$or`, so the next level's leaf scope carries it (`readable-ids-conformance.ts:273-300`). The new conformance case's expected rows check by hand against the fixture (`:99-126`): inner parents {p2 (owner u2), p3 (owner u1, id p3)} → children c2, c3; the empty-reference arm admits c5 (`record_id: null`, `label: 'keep'`); c1, c4, c6, c7 excluded. The analytics raw-SQL path still refuses an uncomposed leaf (`read-scope-sql.ts:8-12`, `:1059`, the finder walks `$or` arrays) and the engine-bound door admits it (`service-analytics/src/plugin.ts:1088-1091`) — unchanged posture.
- *Relation resolver.* `security-plugin-cbp-relation.ts:164-172`: a required candidate still wins; with none, `controlledByParentMasterOf` over the registry field map picks the only `master_detail` declared `required: false`, the reference read with the same tolerant spelling; `optional: candidates.length === 0` (`:225`); an omitted `required` on an unparsed object is `undefined !== false`, so it resolves none and every read is denied (the ADR's fail-closed boundary). `reportCbpMasterUnresolved` names both spellings for a single non-required master (`:254-267`).
- *Writes unchanged.* No write-gate or validation file is in the diff. `security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts:312-313` (an update body that empties the reference) and `:476-477` (an insert with no master, a by-id write on a null-fk row) still throw `MasterReferenceMissingError` (`errors.ts:289-292`: `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD`, 422); for an optional master `omissionRefusedByValidation` is `false` (`security-plugin-cbp-relation.ts:215-216`), so the gate, not record validation, answers — same code either way. Pinned at `controlled-by-parent-optional-master.test.ts:1054-1071`.
- *Spec.* `controlled-by-parent-master.ts:168-179`: one required → that; more than one required → none; else exactly one `master_detail` with `required === false` → optional; `required` omitted, non-boolean, two non-required, or a required `lookup` only → none. `controlledByParentMasterRefusal:206-290` judges through it: the `master-not-writable` arm covers the optional master (`:211-230`); the `several-masters` / `master-not-required` / `required-lookup-only` / `no-master` shapes stand with messages naming both spellings. `object.zod.ts:4109` runs the refinement on the parse. `forceCbpMasterDetailRequired:4514-4547`: `required: true` kept; `required: false` kept only on the object's only `master_detail` (`:4530`), refused beside another with a message naming the other (`:4531-4543`); omitted → forced `true` (`:4544-4545`) — the force half is unchanged, as is `cbp-master-detail-required-defaulted.ts`. `refused-shapes.ts:148-161` retires the explicit-false arm (what is left is a non-boolean `required`, which the field parse refuses on its own; an omitted one is converted by the chain first), and the `master-not-writable` fate names the optional master (`:172-177`). D3 entry `18.cbp-optional-master-admitted.ts` registered at `registry.ts.template:1321-1332` (order 119, unique); the sibling entries it names (`cbp-master-relation-tiers-retired`, `cbp-master-detail-required-forced`) exist. `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` carry the two new exports. The recorded divergence (raw `required === false` vs the parse's defaulted `false`) is pinned in `controlled-by-parent-master.test.ts:1940-1954`, `object.test.ts:2373-2394`, `validate-security-posture.test.ts:484-502`, `controlled-by-parent-sharing.test.ts:1165-1192`.
- *Lint.* `data-model-rules.ts:407-435`: `relationship/master-detail-required` passes the only `master_detail` declared `required: false`, reports `readonly`/`system` on it, reports an omitted or non-boolean `required` on the sole one at `error` naming both spellings, and judges `false` beside another as before; `masterDetailCount` is read from the object's own field list (`:1052`). `validate-security-posture.ts:413-427`: `cbpMasterCandidates` returns the required masters, else the spec resolver's optional one, so `security-controlled-by-parent-no-relation` is silent on a valid optional master and still fires on two non-required masters and on an omitted `required` (the parse/lint divergence pinned at `validate-security-posture.test.ts:484-502`). `rule-explanations.ts:716-735` (`security-controlled-by-parent-no-relation`) and `:3302-3340` (`relationship/master-detail-required`, the optional-master paragraph at `:3318`) teach it. No runtime string in the diff carries a tracker number.
- *objectql boot.* `engine-readable-ids-permission-formula.ts:218-226`: `findUnservableControlledByParentMasters` resolves the master through `controlledByParentMasterOf`, so an optional-master detail is judged for an uncomposable master too; docblocks at `engine-top-level.ts:4931-4935` and `engine.ts:1650-1663` say so.
- *ADR-0055.* Additions only (the ADR hunk has no removed line): a status-line entry (`:8`), inline notes under §1 (`:40`) and §2 (`:52`), and the amendment section (`:200-233`). The amendment's statements match the code read above: the arm shapes, View All confined to the null arm, the queue row and the no-`owner_id` object as View All's alone, the chain rule, the fail-closed boundaries, §3 unchanged. One sentence is stale (must-fix 2).
- *The ui test-only commit 469499ed.* Five files, all `*.test.ts(x)`, +87/-29, no Studio source. The four control legs now assert that the omitted shape parses with `required: false` before Studio writes `required: true`, and with `required: true` after (`object-fields-io.test.ts:412-420`, `ObjectFieldInspector…:111-123`, `ObjectSettingsPanel…:59-63`, `:77-79`, `PackageOwdOverviewPanel…:105-109`, `:125-127`); the two display rows (`owd-sharing.test.ts:66-71`, `:92-95`; `PackageOwdOverviewPanel…:67-72`, `:85-88`) record that the parse admits the omitted shape while the reader names no master — ruling A, encoded correctly; the "two required masters" rows still expect a refusal.
- *The merge fd6d188b.* `git merge-tree --write-tree` of its two parents reproduces its tree (`d4b233c0…`) exactly: the automatic merge, no hand edits; one file in common (`object.zod.ts`, main's `renamedFrom` refinement), and the diff against the merge base carries only this PR's hunks.
- *Tests and ablations, by reading.* The new suite (`controlled-by-parent-optional-master.test.ts`, 24 cases) runs the real plugin and sharing service over an in-memory double on both read faces. Dropping the null arm reds the injected-shape pin (`:971-985`), "the rep reads … the null-master rows they own" on both faces, the chain case on both faces and the disjoint union — six, as reported. Unconfining the owner arm (dropping the `fk IS NULL` conjunct) makes `ct_eu_mine` (owned by the rep, under an unreadable master) and `nt_eu_mine` visible, so it reds those six plus "a row that NAMES a master is never read through the owner arm" on both faces — eight, as reported. Pins on a required master's leaf, View All's confinement, the queue row, the no-`owner_id` object, the write gate, the resolver and the explain narration are each present.
- *Check-runs on the head, latest per name, at the time of writing.* Green: Lint & Repo Gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI/release & engine gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, the three scoped lint lanes, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Check Changeset, Dogfood Regression Gate, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Plan Test Core shards, Build UI Deps, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs, filter. Pending: Build Core, Test Core 1-4 and 6-8 (5/8 green), Test UI 1-16, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI. Red: none.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec` `minor` — right: two new exports (`controlledByParentMasterOf`, `ControlledByParentMaster`), a shape the parse and the builder now accept, a D3 entry; nothing removed or narrowed; `api-surface` and `export-origins` regenerated.
- `@objectstack/plugin-security` `minor` — right: a behavioural widening on one object shape; `computeControlledByParentFilter`'s new required argument is on a private method, and `security-plugin-cbp-read-filter.ts` is not re-exported from the package index.
- `@objectstack/lint` `minor` — right: one spelling passes, messages reworded, severities unchanged.
- `@objectstack/objectql` `minor` — acceptable: the boot refusal now also judges an optional-master detail whose master the engine cannot compose. The only shape it newly refuses is one the parse refused before and the runtime served as "every read denied"; refusing it at boot is the ADR-0139 D5 posture, not a narrowing of a delivered capability. Recorded here so the reader sees it was judged.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` — right (a new accepted authorable shape, no key added).
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — right. Looked for a narrowing and found none: before this head the sole-master `required: false` shape was refused at `ObjectSchema.create()` and at the parse, listed `[metadata_spec_invalid]` at rest with every read denied, and no reader could read a null-master row (the write gate refused one, and a raw-inserted one matched no `$in`); the required master's leaf is byte-identical; every lint error that fired still fires at `error`. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `ui/` change only tests, so no changeset is owed for them.
